intelligence.enrichment: Bean seed germination requires the right amount of water and air. Water softens the seed coat and enables growth processes, while air in spaces between soil particles supports germination and root growth. Light is not essential for bean seeds and most seeds. Missing water prevents necessary growth processes; excess water prevents access to air; moist soil with air permits bean seed germination whether the pot is in light or dark. The learner correctly applies this rule: Bean seed germination requires the right amount of water and air. Water softens the seed coat and enables growth processes, while air in spaces between soil particles supports germination and root growth. Light is not essential for bean seeds and most seeds. Seeds germinate wherever there is sunlight and a lot of water.
